goal: Publish a .NET MAUI Windows package that runs on a clean customer machine without separately installing .NET or the Windows App SDK runtime.
must_include: Explains that `--self-contained` covers the .NET runtime, while `<WindowsAppSDKSelfContained>true</WindowsAppSDKSelfContained>` covers the Windows App SDK framework/runtime files; both may be needed for a fully self-contained Windows package.
Sets `WindowsAppSDKSelfContained` in the MAUI app project file, not in class library projects, to avoid `GenerateAppManifestFromAppx` failures in non-app projects.
Publishes the MAUI app project, not the solution, with a concrete Windows TFM and x64/x86 runtime identifier or `RuntimeIdentifierOverride` appropriate to the target.
Notes that WinUI/Windows App SDK apps cannot become a single-file EXE; native runtime files remain in the package/output.
must_not: Promises that `PublishSingleFile=true` will produce one working WinUI/MAUI Windows executable.
Uses `AnyCPU` for a self-contained Windows App SDK publish.
Solves the customer prompt by asking every customer to install the .NET Desktop Runtime manually.
acceptable_alternatives: Use Visual Studio's package/publish workflow with equivalent self-contained settings.
Use the winapp CLI's equivalent project packaging route (`winapp pack <app>.csproj --self-contained` plus the matching .NET self-contained MSBuild property/RID) if it fits the build pipeline.
Use an unpackaged self-contained folder for non-Store channels if MSIX is not required.
Install the Windows App SDK redistributable separately only if the app deliberately remains framework-dependent.
solved: The answer clearly separates .NET self-contained and Windows App SDK self-contained deployment and gives project/publish settings that produce a package runnable on a clean machine.
partial: The answer adds only `--self-contained` or only `WindowsAppSDKSelfContained` and misses the other runtime dependency.
notes: The issue discussion confirms that `--self-contained` increased the package with .NET files and `WindowsAppSDKSelfContained` added the Windows App SDK files needed on fresh Windows installations.
